question: According to the World Health Organization, what is the age range for adolescence?
explanation: The WHO defines the adolescent period between the ages of 10 and 19 years, covering both early and late teenage years. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do Nigerian midwives consider local cultural markers of adulthood alongside chronological age?

options.A: Midwives are legally required to perform traditional initiation rites for all teenagers
options.B: Age is completely ignored in all Nigerian health facilities during patient registration
options.C: Chronological age has no relevance whatsoever to human biological development
options.D: Cultural markers dictate how communities view young people and affect health service acceptance

explanation: Community perceptions and cultural rites influence how adolescents seek and receive reproductive health care, making local context vital for effective midwifery practice. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h1)

question: At what age does the peak height velocity of the growth spurt typically occur in females compared to males?

options.A: Earlier in females than in males
options.B: Only after the age of twenty in females
options.C: Much later in females than in males
options.D: At the exact same age in both genders

explanation: Girls generally enter puberty and experience their peak adolescent growth spurt roughly two years earlier than boys do. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h2)

question: A 13-year-old female patient worries about gaining fat around her hips and thighs while her twin brother grows taller and more muscular. What physiological reality explains this?

options.A: An abnormal reaction to increased physical exercise in early adolescence
options.B: An early sign of severe nutritional deficiency requiring immediate hospital admission
options.C: Normal sex-specific differences in body composition changes during puberty
options.D: A pathological hormonal disorder that stops female muscle development entirely

explanation: Puberty causes girls to naturally accumulate more subcutaneous fat around the hips and thighs, whereas boys build more lean muscle mass and bone density. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which hormone is released by the hypothalamus to start the pubertal cascade?
explanation: GnRH is the master hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that signals the pituitary gland to release LH and FSH, starting puberty. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why do many young girls experience irregular menstrual cycles during the first year or two after menarche?

options.A: The ovaries have not yet developed any functional egg follicles
options.B: Immature feedback mechanisms within the HPG axis often lead to anovulatory cycles
options.C: Constant dietary changes in secondary schools disrupt uterine lining shedding
options.D: Severe physical exhaustion from household chores stops hormone production

explanation: Because the HPG hormonal axis takes time to fully mature, early menstrual cycles often occur without ovulation, causing temporary irregularity. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which area of the adolescent brain, responsible for impulse control and planning, is among the last to fully mature?
explanation: The prefrontal cortex develops slowly throughout adolescence and early adulthood, which explains teenagers' evolving abilities in long-term planning and decision-making. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h4)

question: How does the difference in maturation speed between the limbic system and the prefrontal cortex affect adolescent behavior?

options.A: It causes immediate cessation of all physical growth spurts
options.B: It forces teenagers to prefer solitary activities over social gathering
options.C: It creates a tendency toward high-risk actions and intense emotional responses
options.D: It results in permanent loss of memory and complete inability to learn

explanation: Because the emotional limbic system matures before the rational prefrontal cortex, teenagers often experience strong emotions and impulsive risk-taking. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h4)

question: According to Erik Erikson, what is the core psychosocial conflict that defines the adolescent life stage?
explanation: Erikson identified the central task of adolescence as figuring out who one is and where one fits into society, termed identity versus role confusion. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a common psychosocial challenge many Nigerian teenagers face while trying to form their identity?

options.A: Losing all biological capacity to form interpersonal friendships
options.B: Experiencing complete memory loss regarding childhood events
options.C: Suffering from permanent inability to communicate in local languages
options.D: Balancing traditional communal expectations with modern global influences

explanation: Nigerian adolescents navigate the tension between family and cultural traditions and the globalized ideas seen on social media and in schools. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a primary positive function of peer groups during adolescence?

options.A: Permanently stopping all hormonal secretion from the pituitary
options.B: Completely replacing the need for any nutritional intake
options.C: Providing a sense of belonging and building social skills
options.D: Guaranteeing total immunity against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Peers offer social support, companionship, and a safe space to practice adult social skills during teenage years. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h6)

question: A 16-year-old boy feels compelled to join a violent campus group because his friends mock his reluctance. What psychosocial pressure is primarily influencing him?

options.A: Normal hormonal fluctuations of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis
options.B: A standard somatic growth spurt resulting in increased muscle mass
options.C: Negative peer pressure and desire for group acceptance
options.D: An innate cognitive transition into formal operational thinking

explanation: The strong teenage desire to fit in with peers can drive young people toward dangerous behaviors if the peer group promotes harmful activities. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h6)

question: What does the acronym HEADSS commonly stand for in adolescent health assessment?

options.A: Height, Energy, Attitude, Development, Sleep, Strength
options.B: Hormones, Emotions, Anatomy, Disease, Symptoms, Safety
options.C: Heart, Endocrine, Abdomen, Diet, Skin, Skeleton
options.D: Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide

explanation: HEADSS is a structured clinical screening tool used to evaluate key psychosocial areas in the lives of adolescents. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is confidentiality crucial when providing reproductive health services to teenagers in a midwifery clinic?

options.A: It is a legal requirement that allows midwives to bypass parental consent entirely for all procedures
options.B: It encourages adolescents to seek care honestly without fear of being reported or shamed
options.C: It stops the HPG axis from releasing gonadotropin hormones prematurely
options.D: It guarantees that teenagers will never experience peer pressure again

explanation: Confidentiality builds trust, ensuring that teenagers feel safe enough to disclose sensitive health concerns regarding sex, substance use, or mental health. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h7)
